title: Entropy-Driven Structural Phase Transition in Nb$_3$Cl$_8$ via Density Functional Theory and an Effective Model
authors: Chenjie Zhu, Shuai Zhang, Zhong Fang, Zhijun Wang, Quansheng Wu, Hongming Weng
abstract: As a prototypical flat-band cluster Mott insulator on an effective triangular lattice, Nb$_3$Cl$_8$ is a potential candidate for hosting a quantum spin liquid (QSL) state. Nevertheless, a first-order structural phase transition around 90K transforms the high-temperature paramagnetic $α$ phase into the low-temperature nonmagnetic $β$ phase, suppressing the candidate QSL regime of the $α$ phase. To clarify the microscopic origin of this transition, we combine first-principles calculations with an extended Hubbard model to construct a unified free-energy framework. This framework reveals that the transition is jointly driven by phonon and spin entropy: the $α$ phase is stabilized by softer phonons and larger paramagnetic spin entropy, whereas the $β$ phase is favored by interlayer dimerization, which hardens the phonons and quenches the spin entropy through singlet formation. Furthermore, by evaluating the pressure-dependent generalized enthalpy, we provide a thermodynamic explanation for the suppression of the transition under c-axis uniaxial pressure, where stabilizing the $α$ phase may allow the candidate QSL regime of the $α$ phase to be explored at low temperatures.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive free-energy framework combining DFT and an extended Hubbard model to explain the structural phase transition in $	ext{Nb}_3	ext{Cl}_8$. The analysis reveals that this transition is governed by a delicate balance between phonon entropy (stabilizing the high-T phase) and spin entropy/lattice dimerization (favoring the low-T phase). This provides a detailed, multi-faceted understanding of how competing entropic forces dictate material structure.
main_problem: The study aims to clarify the microscopic origin of a first-order structural phase transition in $	ext{Nb}_3	ext{Cl}_8$ around 90 K, which suppresses its potential quantum spin liquid (QSL) state.
main_result: The transition is jointly driven by phonon and spin entropy; high temperatures favor the $\alpha$ phase due to soft phonons and large spin entropy, while low temperatures favor the $ eta$ phase via interlayer dimerization and spin-singlet formation.
method: A unified free-energy framework combining first-principles DFT calculations with an extended Hubbard model is employed to analyze lattice, phonon, and spin contributions separately.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Nb}_3	ext{Cl}_8$, modeled using a low-energy effective Hamiltonian derived from the $2a_1$ orbital manifold. The total free energy incorporates DFT energies, harmonic phonon free energy, and Hubbard model contributions.
key_observables: Helmholtz free energies ($\alpha$ vs $ eta$), phonon frequencies, generalized enthalpy under pressure, and transition temperature ($T_c$).
important_parameters: The critical structural transition temperature ($T_c \approx 113	ext{ K}$), the critical uniaxial pressure for suppression ($\approx 2.6	ext{ GPa}$), and Hubbard parameters ($U, V, t$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include using the harmonic approximation for phonons (neglecting anharmonicity) and treating the low-energy subspace explicitly within the correlated model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phonon dispersions showing softening in $\alpha$ vs. hardening in $ eta$, total free energy crossing curves determining $T_c$, and generalized enthalpy plots demonstrating pressure stabilization of the $\alpha$ phase.
paper_structure: The paper builds a comprehensive free-energy functional by combining DFT results with contributions from lattice vibrations (phonons) and electronic correlations (Hubbard model). It analyzes how entropy terms dictate the stability crossover between the two structural phases ($\alpha \leftrightarrow  eta$) under varying conditions like temperature and pressure.
why_interesting: The explicit coupling of vibrational entropy (phonon softening/hardening) with magnetic spin entropy to drive a structural transition is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in correlated materials, bridging solid-state physics and statistical mechanics.
